# uptimepage Provider

Manage Uptimepage monitors, status pages, status page components and notification channels as code. Monitors cover HTTP, TCP, ICMP ping, DNS, TLS certificate expiry, domain expiry and scripted browser login flows. Every resource supports import, and the provider works against the hosted service or a self-hosted instance.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    uptimepage = {
      source = "uptimepage/uptimepage"
    }
  }
}

provider "uptimepage" {
  # endpoint defaults to https://app.uptimepage.dev (the hosted service).
  # Set it for a self-hosted instance, e.g. https://uptime.example.com.
  # endpoint = "https://uptime.example.com"

  # token may also be supplied via UPTIMEPAGE_TOKEN
  token = var.uptimepage_token

  # org scopes API-token requests to one organization (slug). Required for
  # managing resources with a token. May also be set via UPTIMEPAGE_ORG.
  org = "your-org-slug"
}
```

## What this provider manages

| Resource | What it is |
|----------|------------|
| `uptimepage_target` | A monitor: what to check, how often, and from which regions. |
| `uptimepage_notification_channel` | Where an alert goes. Twelve types: webhook, Slack, Telegram, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, email, PagerDuty, ntfy, Pushover, WhatsApp and SMS. |
| `uptimepage_status_page` | A public status page: subdomain slug, branding and theme. Owner-only. |
| `uptimepage_status_page_component` | A monitor shown on a status page. |

There is one data source, `uptimepage_target`, for reading a monitor that
Terraform does not own.

## Check types

A target sets `check.type` to one of seven values, then fills the matching
nested block:

| `check.type` | What it verifies |
|--------------|------------------|
| `http` | Status code, response body, headers, redirects and request timing. Also runs POST bodies, so it covers JSON-RPC and other API handshakes. |
| `tcp` | A TCP connection opens on a host and port. |
| `ping` | A host answers an ICMP echo request. No port, since an echo is not addressed to one. |
| `dns` | A record resolves and returns the answer you expect. |
| `tls_cert` | Days remaining on a TLS certificate, before it expires. |
| `domain_expiry` | Days remaining on a domain registration, read over RDAP. |
| `flow` | A scripted browser journey, such as a real sign-in, in a headless browser. |

Cron heartbeat monitors are not in the provider. The REST API accepts them
today, so create those through the API or the web UI.

`regions` on a target selects which probe locations run the check.

## Importing existing monitoring

Every resource supports `terraform import`, so an account built by clicking can
be adopted without recreating it.

```shell
terraform import uptimepage_target.api                  0192f3a4-5b6c-7d8e-9f01-23456789abcd
terraform import uptimepage_notification_channel.slack  0192aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee
terraform import uptimepage_status_page.public          0192f3a4-5b6c-7d8e-9f01-23456789abcd
terraform import uptimepage_status_page_component.api   0192f3a4-5b6c-7d8e-9f01-23456789abcd:0192aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee
```

Components import as `status_page_id:target_id`. Everything else imports by its
own id.

Secrets never come back from the API, by design, so set them in config after
importing. On a target that is `check.http.basic_auth` and
`check.http.bearer_token`, or their `_wo` write-only forms on Terraform 1.11 and
later. On a channel it is whichever secret its type uses: the webhook `url` and
`headers`, a `webhook_url`, a Telegram `bot_token`, a PagerDuty `routing_key`,
an ntfy or WhatsApp `access_token`, a Pushover `token` and `user`, or the
`auth_token`, `api_key`, `api_secret` and `api_token` an SMS provider needs.

## Hosted or self-hosted

`endpoint` defaults to the hosted service at `https://app.uptimepage.dev`. Point
it at your own instance to manage a self-hosted deployment with the same
configuration.

## Tokens

Authentication uses an API token, passed as `token` or `UPTIMEPAGE_TOKEN`. Grant
it the least scope the run needs: `targets:write` and `channels:write` cover
monitors and channels, `status_page:write` covers pages and their components,
and `write` implies `read`. Add the `:delete` scopes only if you run
`terraform destroy`. Status-page writes are owner-only. Binding a token to one
organization keeps a leaked token away from your others, and `org` must then
match it.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `endpoint` (String) Base URL of the Uptimepage API. Defaults to https://app.uptimepage.dev. May also be set via the UPTIMEPAGE_ENDPOINT environment variable.
- `org` (String) Organization slug to scope API-token requests to (sent as the X-Uptimepage-Org header). Required for token auth against managed resources. May also be set via the UPTIMEPAGE_ORG environment variable.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) API token (Bearer). Create one from the Uptimepage API tokens page. May also be set via the UPTIMEPAGE_TOKEN environment variable.
